question.text: A train blowing a whistle of frequency <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>320</mn><mo> </mo><mi>Hz</mi></math> approaches an observer standing on the platform at a speed of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>66</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>. The frequency observed by the observer will be (given speed of sound <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>=</mo><mn>330</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>) ______ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>Hz</mi></math>.

solution.text:
Using Doppler's effect, the frequency observed by the observer when the train moves towards the stationary observer is 

fapp=fvv-vs

Given here, vs=330 m s-1 and v=66 m s-1

Putting the values, 

fapp=320330330-66

⇒fapp=400 Hz.
